body: I _think_ it might be related to https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/activerecord/lib/active_record/core.rb#L175

@chancancode Digged a little deeper.

Running the failing case, in https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/activerecord/lib/active_record/core.rb#L175 the value of `hash` is `{:user=>#<User id: 1>}` when I guess it should contain `{:user_id=>1}`.

If this is correct I think the issue lies somewhere [here](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/activerecord/lib/active_record/statement_cache.rb#L81), since `relation.bind_values` returns `[]`. I'm not sure though.

Btw shouldn't the assertion before the last one fail too?

@Agis- the second last example should work, it's documented here: http://edgeapi.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveRecord/QueryMethods.html#method-i-where-label-hash

(for those who are curious – it's handled by https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/activerecord/lib/active_record/relation/predicate_builder.rb#L111)

For the last failing case, I figured out why it's failing. Apparently, AR treats `user` and `badge` as "non-bindables" parameters in the condition, because [they don't map to a real column name](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/activerecord/lib/active_record/relation/query_methods.rb#L975).

What this means is that instead of being sent to the DB as `("...WHERE user_id = ?...",  [15])`, they are eventually resolved somewhere [downstream](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/activerecord/lib/active_record/relation/predicate_builder.rb#L32) and sent to the DB "hardcoded" as something like `("user_id = 15", [])`.

This is fine for the [where](https://gist.github.com/chancancode/61eb76aab57ce5f319fd#file-bug-rb-L60) case in my gist, because it builds the query with the actual parameters (`{user: <User#...>, badge: <Badge#...>}`). However, for the new adequate record case, because we are sending in "stand-in" placeholders (`{user: <ActiveRecord::StatementCache::Substitute#...>, badge: <ActiveRecord::StatementCache::Substitute#...>}`), we end up [generating and caching](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/activerecord/lib/active_record/core.rb#L166-L173) a SQL that looks like "...WHERE user_id = NULL..." with no bindable parameters.

Not sure what's the best way to go about fixing this.. cc @tenderlove @matthewd ?

I guess we need to somehow detect that we can't cache these queries (by checking that the keys in the hash are all "real" column names... seems slow though), or that we need to refactor things so that the "fake" column names get resolved into the real column names earlier.

body: @codeodor do you have an opinions on this too? :)

This indeed was very similar to why I added this line: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/activerecord/lib/active_record/core.rb#L155 to simply short-circuit the caching code, because I could not figure out how to make it bind correctly for the default scopes case that included an association.

However, I am not convinced it was for the same reason, because I don't think my case was due to having an object passed in instead of an ID. It could have been though -- I just couldn't dig that deeply to figure it out.

From my inspections, it seemed like the ID was there and correct before running through the statement caching.

If you are able to figure out how to get that binding correct, we could review the work I did to see if it applies there as well.
